# Resolve AMD Instinct hardware access for validation and support

## Description

Determine how the platform gains physical access to AMD Instinct accelerator
nodes for the ROCm enablement effort, and secure a committed access path.
Today no AMD GPU hardware exists in the CI fleet, and every downstream
requirement — serving validation, runtime productization, and training support
— depends on physical AMD Instinct nodes existing and being reachable.

## Scope

- Evaluate the viable access options: hardware procurement (owned nodes) and
  partner-lab access (shared/partner-hosted AMD Instinct capacity).
- For each option, establish cost, lead time, capacity (number and model of
  accelerators), network/API reachability, and security/compliance constraints.
- Recommend and secure one access path with a committed timeline, including who
  operates the hardware and how workloads are submitted to it.
- Define the acceptance basis the hardware must meet for validation purposes
  (Instinct-class accelerators, driver stack compatible with the ROCm versions
  under test).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written recommendation comparing procurement vs partner-lab access exists,
  covering cost, lead time, capacity, and operational model.
- A committed access path is confirmed with a named owner and an expected
  availability date for AMD Instinct nodes.
- The access path's feasibility for running vLLM serving and PyTorch training
  workloads is confirmed (driver/ROCm stack compatibility, node access
  procedure documented).
- The outcome is communicated to the ROCm serving validation, training support,
  and documentation work so downstream planning can proceed or be deferred.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0, gating prerequisite): physical AMD Instinct nodes are a
  precondition for the validation campaign.
- HLR-3 (P1, gating prerequisite): hardware-backed validation underpins the
  "supported" claim for PyTorch ROCm training.

# vLLM ROCm functional and performance validation campaign on AMD Instinct hardware

## Description

Run a first-hand validation campaign of vLLM ROCm builds on physical AMD
Instinct hardware to establish functional and performance parity data for the
platform's supported model set, and produce the go/no-go scope for
productization. The platform currently ships only CUDA runtime builds and has
no first-hand ROCm parity data.

## Scope

- Pin the supported model set to be validated (the set is not enumerated in
  the strategy and must be confirmed by stakeholders before execution).
- Select the upstream vLLM ROCm image/driver combinations to test.
- For each model in the pinned set, establish:
  - Functional parity: the model loads, serves, and returns correct results
    under the ROCm vLLM build.
  - Performance parity: throughput and latency measurements against a CUDA
    baseline on comparable hardware, with recorded deltas.
- Produce a go/no-go verdict per model: which models clear the bar for
  productization, which fail, and why.
- Publish the results, including hardware/driver configuration used and
  measurement methodology, so the numbers are reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The supported model set under test is pinned and recorded before the campaign
  starts.
- Every model in the pinned set has a recorded functional result (works /
  broken, with failure details) on AMD Instinct hardware.
- Every functionally-clearing model has recorded performance measurements with
  a defined comparison baseline and methodology.
- A go/no-go summary exists listing exactly which models are cleared for
  productization, with supporting data.
- The hardware and driver configuration used for the campaign is documented.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0, direct): this epic is the validation campaign that produces the
  functional/performance parity data and the go/no-go scope.
- HLR-2 (P0, prerequisite): the go/no-go scope this epic produces determines
  which models the productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime ships with.

# Assess upstream ROCm image release cadence against platform release trains

## Description

Determine whether AMD's upstream ROCm runtime image release cadence aligns
with the platform's release trains, and recommend the image sourcing approach
for the productized vLLm ROCm serving runtime. Upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities; whether it aligns with our
trains changes how productization consumes those images.

## Scope

- Inventory how upstream vLLM and the ROCm ecosystem publish ROCm-enabled
  runtime images: release channels, tagging conventions, support windows.
- Compare the upstream cadence and image lifecycle against the platform's
  release train schedule and support policy.
- Identify the alignment gaps: versions skipped, images EOL'd mid-train,
  breaking changes between ROCm releases.
- Recommend a sourcing approach for productization: consume upstream AMD
  releases directly vs build and pin midstream images, including the tradeoffs
  for each against the platform support policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The upstream ROCm image publication model (channels, cadence, lifecycle) is
  documented with sources.
- A comparison against the platform release trains exists, with specific
  alignment gaps identified.
- A recommended sourcing approach for the productized runtime is recorded,
  with rationale, so productization can proceed on a known basis.
- The recommendation states what happens when upstream cadence does not align
  (fallback path).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, gating prerequisite): the sourcing approach determines how the
  supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is built and released.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

Productize a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models cleared by the
validation campaign, delivered through the existing Serving Runtimes
integration so models can be served on AMD Instinct accelerators via KServe
InferenceServices. Today the platform ships only CUDA (NVIDIA) runtime builds;
ROCm builds exist upstream but are not shipped or supported.

## Scope

- Build or adopt (per the resolved upstream cadence assessment) the vLLM ROCm
  runtime image for platform release, pinned and reproducible.
- Define and ship the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime configuration that
  runs the ROCm vLLM build on AMD Instinct nodes, requesting amd.com/gpu
  resources.
- Restrict the supported surface to the models cleared by the validation
  campaign go/no-go.
- Validate that InferenceServices using the ROCm runtime deploy and serve
  correctly through KServe in both serverless and raw deployment modes, on
  AMD Instinct hardware.
- Ensure the runtime image build and release follows the existing per-platform
  release process (Konflux pipeline stays green).
- Establish the support posture for the ROCm runtime relative to the CUDA
  builds (what is supported, what is not).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pinned, reproducible vLLM ROCm runtime image is built through the
  platform's build pipeline for a target release.
- The build pipeline is green for the runtime image.
- A ServingRuntime configuration deploys the ROCm runtime and requests
  amd.com/gpu resources on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Every model in the cleared (go/no-go) set deploys and serves correct
  responses through KServe InferenceServices on AMD Instinct hardware,
  validated in both serverless and raw deployment modes.
- No un-cleared model is presented as supported.
- The support posture for the ROCm serving runtime is documented.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, direct): this epic productizes the supported vLLM ROCm serving
  runtime for the models the validation campaign clears.
- HLR-1 (P0, upstream): consumes the validation campaign's go/no-go scope as
  its input.

# PyTorch ROCm training support in the Training Operator

## Description

Enable PyTorch training on ROCm for single- and multi-GPU jobs run through the
Training Operator, so PyTorchJob workloads execute on AMD Instinct
accelerators. The Training Operator currently runs PyTorchJob jobs against
NVIDIA GPU worker nodes; ROCm-backed training jobs must run and be validated
on physical AMD hardware.

## Scope

- Verify PyTorchJob pods can be scheduled with amd.com/gpu resources on AMD
  Instinct nodes for single-GPU jobs.
- Verify multi-GPU (and multi-node, where the hardware access allows)
  PyTorchJob topologies run on ROCm: distributed launch, device discovery, and
  job completion.
- Confirm the PyTorch ROCm runtime images usable by training jobs (base images
  or documented image requirements) for the platform.
- Validate functional correctness of representative single- and multi-GPU
  training jobs on AMD Instinct hardware.
- Record the supported job shapes and any ROCm-specific limitations found.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu runs to completion on AMD
  Instinct hardware.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob runs to completion on AMD Instinct hardware with
  correct distributed-training behavior.
- Functional validation results for representative training jobs on physical
  AMD hardware are recorded.
- The supported PyTorch ROCm image basis for training jobs is documented.
- Any ROCm-specific job limitations discovered during validation are recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, direct): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs.
